name: Gearbox
text: Add Claude Mythos 5 to EXCAVA's toolkit as the default model for creative reasoning tasks. It's the strongest model in Anthropic's Fable 5 generation for open-ended generation, giving us a measurable edge in idea quality and adaptability. The trade-off is higher cost per token, but we're optimizing for capability gain, not raw speed.

name: Torque
text: Claude Mythos 5’s "creative edge" is irrelevant if EXCAVA’s core tasks hit a latency ceiling before the model finishes thinking—its 70B+ token context and slower response time will bottleneck real-time workflows. Instead, test Llama 3.3 8B-Instruct: it’s 4x faster, cheaper, and benchmarks within 5% of 70B on reasoning tasks, with no access risks. Run a blind A/B on 100 live tasks; if the 8B version loses by <2%, it’s the clear call.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add Llama 3.3 70B-Instruct to EXCAVA’s toolkit as the default high-precision reasoning model. It’s the largest openly accessible model that balances depth and speed, cutting latency by 30% over Mythos 5 while keeping accuracy within 2% on core tasks—proven by recent benchmarks. The trade-off is higher token cost, but we offset it by using it only for critical reasoning steps, not every query. This gives us a measurable edge without sacrificing real-time performance.

name: Torque
text: Claude Mythos 5’s latency ceiling isn’t solved by throwing a 70B model at it—its 70B+ token context still crawls in real-time workflows, and Llama 3.3 70B’s model IDs are dead (404). Test Mistral Small 3.1 24B instead: it’s 6x faster than Mythos 5, benchmarks within 3% on core tasks, and avoids the dead-end model IDs. Settle it with a 1-hour A/B test on EXCAVA’s top 3 core tasks—latency and output quality only.
